oneLiner: A flat-revenue car and storage business with a 2-3% operating margin, valued as if it were an autonomy and robotics platform. The market is betting that unsupervised robotaxi and Optimus turn into revenue in 2027-2028, before the AI spend finishes eating the car profits.

verdict.summary: Q3 2026 was a relief print, not a turn: a small non-GAAP beat, positive free cash flow because capex came in below plan, and real autonomy progress (Cybercab rides in Austin, ~2M unsupervised miles). Revenue is flat, operating margin is under 3% and opex is still rising ~40% a year, and the price needs earnings to compound far faster than the business has ever grown revenue. Our base case (a modest margin recovery and the multiple held at a very high level) is worth about what the stock trades at today. The bear case needs only for the autonomy timeline to slip again, and that has happened every year since 2019, so the skew is negative. Two things would change the view: unsupervised service scaling to a four-digit fleet across several metros by mid-2027, or operating margin back above 5% while R&D keeps climbing.
wtb: FY2027 revenue grows at least 10% (to ~$116B+ on FY2026's ~$106B) as battery supply unlocks the backlog Tesla calls its largest in four years.
Unsupervised FSD in customer-owned cars launches on the Q2 2027 date, and the unsupervised fleet passes ~1,000 vehicles across 5+ metros by end of Q2 2027.
GAAP operating margin is back above 5% by Q4 2027 even with R&D growing faster than revenue.
At end-2027 the market still pays ~140x FY2027 EPS, which requires visible autonomy and Optimus revenue in the FY2028 numbers.

bear.why: The backlog fades once battery supply catches up, energy deployments stay flat, and BYD pricing forces another price-cut cycle. Revenue slips ~5%. Non-GAAP net margin stays near 5% as SI, Optimus and Cybercab R&D keep rising. Unsupervised customer FSD slips past Q2 2027 again, so the market starts valuing Tesla closer to a growth automaker with options. 80x is still double any auto peer.

base.why: Vehicle volume grows high single digits and energy and services compound. Revenue rises ~11%. Gross margin holds near 20% and opex growth slows, so net margin recovers to ~7%. Robotaxi reaches several metros with a few thousand vehicles: real, but immaterial to revenue. The narrative holds the multiple near today's level.

bull.why: Customer-car unsupervised FSD ships on time and Cybercab volume ramps in 2027, so FSD and fleet revenue start to show. Megafactory Texas lifts storage, and revenue grows ~27%. Software mix takes net margin to ~9.5%. With FY2028 autonomy revenue visible, the multiple expands.

scenarioModel.note: FY2026 revenue assumes Q1 $22.4B + Q2 $28.2B + Q3 $28.0B + ~$27B Q4 = ~$106B. EPS = revenue x non-GAAP net margin / ~3.6B diluted shares (3.54B in Q3 2026 plus CEO award dilution). Bear 100 x 5.0% / 3.6 = $1.39; base 118 x 7.0% / 3.6 = $2.29; bull 135 x 9.5% / 3.6 = $3.56. Non-GAAP (ex stock comp) is the basis consensus uses; Q3 2026 non-GAAP net margin was 6.1%. Multiples are applied to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Does unsupervised autonomy scale in 2027, or slip again?
debates.bull: Cybercab rides started in Austin on Sep 3, cumulative unsupervised miles rose eightfold q/q to nearly 2M, and unsupervised service now runs beyond Texas (Miami, Orlando, Tampa per the Q2 call). Customer cars join the fleet in Q2 2027.
debates.bear: The Q2 2027 'unsupervised' product is narrower than promised: owners add cars to Tesla's managed fleet, in Tesla's zones. Personal unsupervised use was promised for end-2025. Fleet size is still undisclosed, and the NHTSA FSD probe is open.
debates.view: This debate sets the multiple, 80x versus 180x. Miles are progress, but the number that matters is fleet size, and Tesla does not report it. We hold the base case until a fleet count is disclosed.

signpost.metric: Disclosed unsupervised robotaxi fleet size and metros; customer-car unsupervised launch
signpost.threshold: bullish if 1,000+ vehicles in 5+ metros and the Q2 2027 launch holds; bearish if the launch slips past Q2 2027
signpost.when: Q4 2026 report (late Jan 2027) through Q2 2027 report (late Jul 2027)

debates.q: Is the margin trough behind us?
debates.bull: Total gross margin recovered to 19.6% from 16.8% in Q2, auto gross margin ex credits rose to 18.1%, energy margin bounced to 33%, and the order backlog lets Tesla run its factories at full utilization.
debates.bear: Q3's 2.6% operating margin is still less than half the year-ago 5.8%. Opex grew 39% and R&D 69% in Q3 as SI, Optimus and Cybercab spending ramps, and regulatory credits ($113M, down 73%) are not coming back.
debates.view: Gross margin has stabilized. Opex is the problem, and it is a choice management keeps making. The base case needs opex growth to halve in 2027. If it does not, base-case EPS is too high.

signpost.metric: GAAP operating margin and opex growth YoY
signpost.threshold: bullish if operating margin is above 4% with opex growth under 25%; bearish if operating margin is below 2%

debates.q: How much cash does the AI build-out consume?
debates.bull: $45.4B of cash and investments plus $6.3B of Q3 operating cash flow fund the plan without dilution, and FCF was positive again in Q3.
debates.bear: The >$25B 2026 capex guide implies ~$12B in Q4 against a record quarter of $5.8B. Either spend slips into 2027 or FCF turns sharply negative, and Q3's positive FCF came from under-spending, not earnings.
debates.view: The balance sheet can absorb it. The issue is that 2027 capex will probably exceed 2026's, which pushes FCF payback further out while the price already assumes it.

signpost.metric: FY2027 capex guidance vs trailing operating cash flow (~$19B)
signpost.threshold: bearish if 2027 capex is guided above $30B with no revenue timeline attached

thesis: Software is starting to show up in the P&L. Active FSD subscriptions (including upfront purchases) reached 1.74M (+67% YoY), FSD is attached to over 75% of new North American deliveries, and services and other posted record gross profit of $734M.

Autonomy has real miles now. Cybercab entered paid service in Austin and unsupervised miles grew eightfold in a quarter, the first evidence that the camera-only stack runs without a safety driver at more than demo scale.
The balance sheet funds the bet. Cash and investments of $45.4B and positive Q3 free cash flow mean the AI and robotics program needs no equity, unlike most of the autonomy field.
Energy is a second growth engine. Megafactory Texas (50 GWh planned) began production, and storage gross margin recovered to ~33% from 20% in Q2 after warranty and tariff items rolled off.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep; reported Oct 21, 2026)
points: Revenue $28.05B, flat YoY and in line with ~$28.06B consensus; automotive $20.56B (-3%), energy $2.88B (-16%), services and other $4.61B (+33%).
Non-GAAP EPS $0.48 vs $0.45 consensus (vs $0.50 a year ago); GAAP EPS $0.22, net income $787M (-43%), including a $288M bitcoin gain and a $142M SpaceX mark-down.
Gross margin 19.6%; GAAP operating income $718M (-56% YoY), operating margin 2.6%; opex $4.78B (+39%), R&D $2.76B (+69%), stock comp $1.17B.
Operating cash flow $6.26B, capex $4.73B, FCF $1.53B; cash and investments $45.4B.
Deliveries 486,532 (-2% YoY), production 464,391; storage deployed 13.7 GWh (+10%); regulatory credits $113M (-73%).

latestProse: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 21). Revenue $28.05B, flat YoY, with automotive down 3% and energy down 16% (partly tariff-related customer refunds), offset by services and other up 33%. Gross margin recovered to 19.6% (16.8% in Q2), and auto gross margin ex credits rose to 18.1%. Opex grew 39% to $4.78B on Super Intelligence (SI) compute, Optimus and Cybercab R&D plus the CEO award, so GAAP operating income fell 56% to $718M (2.6% margin). Non-GAAP EPS of $0.48 beat by three cents. GAAP net income was flattered by a $288M unrealized bitcoin gain. Free cash flow was $1.53B, but only because capex ($4.73B) ran well below the full-year plan. Deliveries beat consensus (~462K) and days of supply fell to 11, but storage deployments (13.7 GWh) missed the ~15.9 GWh expected. On the product side, Cybercab rides began Sep 3 in Austin, Optimus started on high-volume lines in Fremont, and Semi volume production began in Nevada.
guidanceProse: Tesla gave no numeric delivery, revenue or margin guidance. The letter says it is running factories at maximum utilization against its largest passenger-vehicle backlog in four years, limited by battery supply. It also plans 400 MW of SI training compute by year-end and Austin fab commissioning in 2027. The 2026 capex guide of 'over $25 billion' (set on the Q1 call) was not updated. Nine-month capex was $13.01B, which leaves an implausible ~$12B for Q4. A report that the CFO cut the guide to $20B is unverified, and some spend will probably slip into 2027. The company's autonomy date moved again: unsupervised FSD in customer-owned cars is now Q2 2027, framed as owners adding their cars to Tesla's managed robotaxi fleet within its zones (Electrek, call commentary).

guide.label: FY26 capex guide
guide.sub: No volume or margin guidance | 9M capex $13.0B | customer unsupervised FSD Q2 2027

segments: Automotive ~73% of revenue ($20.56B in Q3 2026, -3% YoY): volume constrained by battery supply, not demand. Model S/X ended in 2026 to free Fremont for Optimus. Regulatory credits are fading out.
Energy generation and storage ~10% ($2.88B in Q3 2026, -16%): 13.7 GWh deployed, segment gross margin ~33%, Megafactory Texas ramping toward 50 GWh.
Services and other ~16% ($4.61B in Q3 2026, +33%): Supercharging, insurance and FSD (1.74M active subscriptions including upfront purchases), record $734M gross profit.
competitive: BYD sets world EV prices and out-produces Tesla in BEVs. It is the reason a backlog has not translated into higher selling prices.
Waymo runs the largest deployed driverless fleet in the US by an order of magnitude. Tesla's counter is cost per vehicle (camera-only Cybercab), not yet scale.
Rivian R2 targets Model Y's core segment with a brand that does not carry Musk's political baggage.
GM and Ford hybrid pivots absorb post-credit US demand that would otherwise go to Tesla.
AI labs, including Musk's own xAI (in which Tesla invested $2B), compete with Tesla's SI program for compute, talent and capital.
moat: Manufacturing scale, the Supercharger network and a multi-million-vehicle fleet that feeds driving data are real advantages. The FSD attach rate shows software pricing power rivals lack. The car moat is eroding on cost (BYD) and brand. The AI-era moat, robotaxi and Optimus, now has evidence (paid Cybercab rides, ~2M unsupervised miles, a high-volume Optimus line) but no disclosed scale.
risks: The bar is far above the track record. The reverse DCF needs forward earnings to compound ~39% a year for a decade, against ~5% a year revenue growth over the last three fiscal years, and the multiple leaves no room for another timeline slip.

Opex is outrunning gross profit. Operating margin fell from ~6% to 1.4% over four quarters to Q2 2026 and was only 2.6% in Q3, with R&D +69% YoY. That spend is committed, while the revenue it is meant to produce is not.

Capex is stepping up with no revenue attached. Capex/revenue has risen from ~9% in 2022 to ~12.5% TTM and is heading higher on the >$25B plan. 2027 capex is likely larger, and Q3 FCF was positive only because spend lagged plan.

Autonomy timelines and regulators. Unsupervised personal use has slipped from end-2025 to a narrower Q2 2027 product. NHTSA's FSD engineering analysis (~3.2M vehicles, degraded-visibility crashes) and China's 2.98M-vehicle door-handle recall show regulatory exposure in both flagship markets.

Governance is part of the valuation. The ~$1T CEO award (path to ~29% ownership, $1.17B of Q3 stock comp including it) and Tesla's $2B xAI stake tie the AI narrative to the CEO's other companies, and brand backlash still weighs on European demand.
catalysts: Early Jan 2027: Q4 2026 deliveries - whether battery supply lets volume grow off the backlog (debate 2).
Late Jan 2027: Q4 2026 report - operating margin, opex growth, and the first 2027 capex framing (debates 2 and 3).
Through 1H 2027: robotaxi metro launches and any first disclosure of fleet size; NHTSA FSD probe rulings (debate 1).
Q2 2027: guided launch of unsupervised FSD for customer-owned cars in Tesla's robotaxi zones (debate 1).
2027: Cybercab and Optimus volume ramps, Semi high-volume output in Nevada, Austin fab commissioning (debate 3).

valPresets.note: Forward-EPS basis because trailing GAAP earnings are depressed by the AI spend cycle and the market is explicitly paying for the future. The reverse DCF shows the implied growth (~39% a year for a decade), which even the bull preset does not reach.
